newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs demand urgent clampdown on sex tourism.
newsitem.headline: MEPs demand urgent clampdown on sex tourism.

text.p: In the wake of the child sex abuse scandals which rocked Belgium this summer, the European Parliament on Friday demanded urgent European Union action to combat sex tourism.
Euro-MPs asked the EU to include special measures to stamp out sex tourism in its 1997-2000 Philoxenia programme to promote the European tourist industry.

In a separately move, MEPs approved a European Commission report on the 1993-1995 action plan to help the EU tourist industry -- COM(96)166 -- and a Commission communication on measures affecting toursim in 1994 -- COM(96)29.

While they approved the new Philoxenia programme -- COM(96)168 -- MEPs insisted it should go further than its declared aims of improving the quality of Europe's tourism industry, boosting jobs in the sector and protecting the environment.

In a report drafted by Spanish Christian Democrat Francisca Bennasar Tous, the Parliament said the European Commission's promise to publish a discussion paper on child sex tourism by the end of the year was not enough.
The Commission should think about concrete action now, MEPs said.
The Commission hoped to present a report discussing possible measures early next month, EU commissioner for tourism Christos Papoutsis told the Parliament on Tuesday.
He said that recent tragic events in Belgium, where four young girls were abused and murdered by a paedophile gang, had given impetus to calls for an EU-wide crack-down.
Parliament wants the Philoxenia tourism programme to fund a study of the geographic, economic, legal and cultural factors which encourage sex tourism.

MEPs said this analysis should form the basis of a well-targeted strategy to fight the dark underside of the tourist industry - child rape, prostitution, trafficking in human beings, pornography and its distribution through the Internet.
They also urged the Commission to use funds from Philoxenia for an EU-wide advertising campaign condemning sex tourism.
Although Europe is still the world's major tourist destination, its leadership is being increasingly challenged.
MEPs said Europe needed to clamp down on sub-standard tourist accommodation and start catering more accurately for specific categories of tourist such as the elderly, the young and the handicapped.
Bennasar Tous chairs the Parliament's all party "Family, Children and Solidarity" group.
